subject: Structured discount bridge + technical packaging for Optimize guidance
messages:
From: Samantha Green <samantha.green@finflux.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Wu <alex.wu@finflux.com>, Finflux Procurement <procurement@finflux.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow on Optimize recommendations and pricing

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the demo last week. Finflux is very interested in the cost/perf angle you showed for high-throughput scoring (tokens/sec matters a lot for batch re-ranking). Procurement asked me to get a clearer picture of how Redwood would structure pricing if we plan to start with a 3-month pilot and then scale to a 12-month committed band.

Couple of asks up front:
- Can you outline a pilot offer (credits, observability retention, ops support) and the follow-on committed discount tiers?
- We also need a short technical note on quantization and caching recommendations so our infra folks can sign off.

Appreciate a concise proposal I can share with Procurement.

Thanks,
Samantha
Head of ML Product, Finflux
[External]

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@finflux.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow on Optimize recommendations and pricing

Hi Samantha —

Great to hear — glad the demo landed. I can do a focused proposal this afternoon. High-level summary while I pull the doc together:

Pilot (90 days):
- $30k in platform credits to cover initial inference and evals.
- Access to Optimize toolkit (batching/caching suggestions) and a 1:1 session with an ML performance engineer.
- 14-day observability retention + SLO onboarding.

Follow-on (12-month committed):
- Tiered discounts based on committed monthly token spend: 10% at $1k/day, 18% at $5k/day, 25% at $15k/day.
- Add-on: Quantization advisory (model quantization, validation corpus run) included for first model.

Technical note (short): recommend int8 quantization + prefix KV caching for your re-ranker flows; avoid aggressive sequence-length-driven batching on short queries to keep latency predictable. I will attach a one-pager and a draft SOW.

I'll loop Ben and Rishi inside our team to confirm ops/finance flex. Expect a PDF and numbers in next message.

Best,
Lauren
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Quantization_Benefits_1pager.pdf (PDF, 42KB)]

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 13:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Finflux pilot -> need guidance on discount structure and packaging

Ben / Rishi —
Forwarding Finflux ask. Key constraints: they want a low-friction 90-day pilot then a clear bridge to committed pricing. Ops will need the quant + caching note (link attached).

Questions:
1) Can we compress the tiers so legal signs a 12-month commit but with an initial 60-day low-usage ramp before higher commit counts kick in? That would protect their budget and get us runway.
2) Any room for an initial higher credit ($45k instead of $30k) if they take a 6-month partial commit (50% of anticipated tokens)?

My suggested approach: structured discount bridge — pilot credits + milestone-triggered discounts (milestone = production traffic threshold + quality gate). If we do that, what internal approvals do we need?

Thanks — quick replies welcome.

Lauren

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 14:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Finflux pilot -> need guidance on discount structure and packaging

Sounds reasonable. A few operational notes:
- We can offer $45k credits if they commit to a 6-month partial commit (50% of expected monthly tokens) but require a 30% non-refundable portion applied as a prepayment to reduce churn risk.
- For the 12-month commit bands, we should cap max discount at 28% to preserve margin at scale.
- Include automatic fallback policies: if quantization causes >3% degradation on eval set, we pause auto-quant and escalate with the ML eng team — limits our risk.

I'll flag this with Finance for quick greenlight on the 45k credit prepay model.

Ben

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Finflux pilot -> need guidance on discount structure and packaging

Agree with Ben. A couple of clarifications to include in the external proposal:
- Quantization recommendation: run int8 evaluation on a representative validation set + perf sweep with KV cache enabled. Typical result for similar customers: 40-55% token-cost reduction with <2% quality drift.
- Batching/caching guidance: set continuous batching target at 40-60ms queue latency for scoring flows, enable prefix caching for top-100k prefixes and a per-model KV window of 32k entries.
- Ops/Support: include one production runbook handover and two weeks of on-call overlap during initial rollout.

I'll prepare the technical appendix; please attach it to the SOW.

Rishi

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@finflux.com>
Cc: Alex Wu <alex.wu@finflux.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, Finflux Procurement <procurement@finflux.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposal: 90-day pilot + structured discount bridge (Finflux)

Hi Samantha / Alex / Procurement —

Thanks for the patience while we consolidated internally. Attached is a concise proposal and SOW draft; summary below so you can share quickly with Procurement.

Proposal highlights (concise):
- Pilot: 90 days, $45k in platform credits (covers eval runs + first two models), 1x ML performance session, 14-day observability retention, runbook handover.
- Path to commit: sign 12-month agreement with milestone-based discount bridge: 12% baseline, 20% after milestone 1 (50% of expected throughput), 28% at full expected throughput. Milestones are time-bound (90/180 days) or traffic-bound, whichever comes first.
- Payment structure: 30% of the 12-month committed value is invoiced up front as a non-refundable credit to reduce churn risk; remaining invoiced monthly.
- Quantization & caching: we recommend an int8 evaluation + KV prefix caching (see attached one-pager). If quantization causes >3% quality regression, we pause auto-quant and deliver remediation at no extra charge.
- Ops & SLOs: 2-week overlap support, one post-launch runbook, and access to our Optimize recommendations dashboard.

Attachments included: Finflux_SOW_draft.pdf, Quantization_Benefits_1pager.pdf, batching-cache-ops.xlsx

Next steps we suggest:
1) Procurement to confirm the 30% prepay acceptance or propose alternative (letter of credit?).
2) Technical team to confirm int8 evaluation dataset (we can provide a checklist).
3) If agreed, we prepare signatures and schedule a kickoff (within 5 business days).

Happy to hop on a short call today to walk Procurement through the structure.

Best,
Lauren
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachments: Finflux_SOW_draft.pdf, Quantization_Benefits_1pager.pdf, batching-cache-ops.xlsx]

From: Finflux Procurement <procurement@finflux.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Green <samantha.green@finflux.com>, Alex Wu <alex.wu@finflux.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: 90-day pilot + structured discount bridge (Finflux)

Hello Lauren —

Procurement has reviewed the high-level terms. A few items we need clarified / adjusted before we can recommend to legal:
- The 30% up-front non-refundable prepay is a hard ask for our CFO. Can you split that into 15% prepay + 15% held as performance guarantee (returnable on milestone completion)?
- We need an explicit SLA credit line for availability (<99.5% eligible for credit) and incident response times for the pilot.
- Discount ceiling: is 28% the firm maximum? Can you confirm if there is any flexibility for enterprise account pricing with a committed increase after 6 months?

If you can respond to those three items, we can push to legal and target signature within two weeks.

Regards,
Procurement Team, Finflux
[External]

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Finflux Procurement <procurement@finflux.com>, Samantha Green <samantha.green@finflux.com>, Alex Wu <alex.wu@finflux.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2026 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: 90-day pilot + structured discount bridge (Finflux)

Hi Procurement team —

Thanks — quick answers below and happy to formalize in the SOW: 

1) Payment split: we can accept 15% prepay + 15% as a performance guarantee that becomes refundable once milestone 1 (50% expected throughput and quality gate) is met. We'll add clear milestone acceptance criteria to the SOW.

2) SLA credits: for the pilot we will add a limited SLA schedule: availability target 99.0% (pilot) with credits triggered below 99.0% and 99.5% for the committed term. For the 12-month commit we will target 99.5% and include standard SLA credits (specified percent of monthly invoice). We'll add incident response time commitments for P1/P2 in the SOW.

3) Discount ceiling flexibility: 28% is our standard ceiling in the published bands; we can re-evaluate after 6 months if total committed spend increases by 40% or more — in that case Finance will consider an incremental top-up to the discount band.

If those look acceptable, I will update the SOW and circulate a redline-ready doc for legal review. We can also schedule a short call with Finance if they'd like to review the prepay / guarantee mechanics.

Thanks and looking forward —
Lauren
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Updated_SOW_terms_summary.txt]
